newsitem.title: MONGOLIA: Mongolia inflation rises in February.
newsitem.headline: Mongolia inflation rises in February.

text.p: Mongolia's consumer price inflation rose 3.2 percent in February over the previous month, the State Statistical Office said.
Inflation in January-February was up 5.6 percent from the beginning of the year, the office said in a report late on Friday.
Mongolia's consistently high inflation was caused by clumsy intervention in currency markets by the Bank of Mongolia, the central bank, a banking conference concluded on Friday.
The bank's failure to stop leaks of classified information about monetary policy were also factors in skyrocketing prices, one bank official who attended the meeting told Reuters.
The weakness of Mongolia's currency, the tugrik, has helped spur the rampant inflation, with the official exchange rate nearing 850 tugriks to the dollar against 680 to the dollar in early January.
Mongolia has set an annual inflation target of about 35 percent for 1997.
The State Statistical Office said that annual inflation for 1996 was 53.2 percent but the central bank estimated it at 58.7 percent.
In 1995, prices rose by 53.1 percent, compared with 66.3 percent in 1994, 183 percent in 1993 and 325.5 percent in 1992, official figures show.
